## What's new

Threadnote 5.4.3 updates managed Codex MCP entries to use the active release after an install or update.

### Codex connections after an update

An open Codex chat can still use its previous connection. If a refresh is pending, Threadnote explains how to reconnect.

If you have a supported private Codex app-server socket, run this command to request an MCP reload.

```sh
threadnote repair --mcp codex \
  --codex-reload-socket /absolute/path/to/owner.sock \
  --codex-reload-thread LOADED_CHAT_ID
```

### Context Brief and recall

If a scoped graph status check times out, Context Brief can show a small set of results from a ready snapshot. It marks those results as stale. Until it can verify freshness, Context Brief withholds exact source excerpts and claims about what the scope excludes.

If any read cannot confirm index maintenance, recall keeps that warning when it combines the results.

### PR watch recovery

You can process queued notices after a PR watch stops. If the PR head changes, a notice that has already arrived can still resume its original task.

If GitHub changes the base branch of a stacked PR, Threadnote verifies the merge and any required maintenance evidence before it completes the task.

If a spawned Codex agent cannot receive notices, Threadnote tells you to start future watches from the owning top-level chat.
